interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s renewable fleet is performing near peak operational capacity, with wind assets currently delivering a robust 4.4 GW into the transmission network. This immense green output has driven regional carbon intensity down to an exceptional 32 gCO2/kWh, underscoring Scotland’s role as the primary engine for Great Britain’s clean power delivery during favorable meteorological conditions. 

However, enduring transmission boundary bottlenecks—notably along the B6 cross-border corridor—continue to restrict optimal power evacuation toward high-demand southern load centers. Consequently, the system has logged 217.5 MWh of wasted energy, driven by active curtailment directives through the Balancing Mechanism to protect local network stability. While these actions preserve grid integrity, the curtailment of zero-marginal-cost electricity exposes ongoing economic friction in the form of constraint costs and network congestion. 

To alleviate this recurring dispatch paradox, system planners must accelerate cross-border interconnector reinforcements while scaling up co-located battery energy storage systems (BESS) and dynamic industrial demand response north of the border. Although the current telemetry demonstrates world-class decarbonization performance, capturing the full economic and operational value of future generation peaks depends on unlocking this trapped renewable capacity.
